statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-95838 (GO-2026-6796, GHSA-rp3h-jf77-q9p4): containerd's layer unpack handler walked the directory tree again for every opaque whiteout in a layer, so pulling or importing a crafted image can take superlinear time and CPU during unpacking. It is fixed in containerd 2.3.5, 2.2.8, 2.0.12 and 1.7.35 by a change to applyNaive in containerd's pkg/archive package (https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-rp3h-jf77-q9p4, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6796, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/e6ca378dcfa610d06589a3ac96aa992de866e4f0 on main, https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/45166eb828c9f8605db44299836a87b78bda701b on release/2.2). Read the Go build information and the function table (with a reader of the Go symbol table that also works on stripped binaries) of every Go program in every build-dev package published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository: 89 builds, 2.6.4-r0 through the current 2.29.1-r1, each for x86_64 and aarch64 except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only, every download checked against the index checksum. Version 2.19.1-r1 is listed three times in each index; the copy the repository serves, which matches one of those entries' checksum, was read. Each package holds one file, the frontend Go program /usr/bin/build. runtime.main is found in the function table of every Go program scanned, so the tables were read. The build information of the frontend program lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 through v2.3.7 across the builds, but the vulnerable code is not linked in. In every build, the only containerd packages in its function table are core/remotes/docker, core/remotes/docker/auth, core/remotes/errors, internal/lazyregexp, pkg/identifiers, pkg/reference and version (all under github.com/containerd/containerd/v2), and no function table of any Go program in any build contains a function from containerd's pkg/archive package. As a positive control, the same reader lists pkg/archive functions, including github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/pkg/archive.applyNaive, in /usr/bin/containerd from the DHI containerd 2.4.2-r5 package. The vulnerable code is not present in this package, so the containerd version recorded in its build information does not make it affected.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-95838 (GHSA-rp3h-jf77-q9p4, GO-2026-6796): containerd's layer unpacker, applyNaive in the archive package, walked a directory again for every opaque whiteout entry in it, so a crafted image layer that interleaves files and opaque whiteouts makes unpacking take superlinear time and CPU. It is fixed in containerd 2.3.5, 2.2.8, 2.0.12 and 1.7.35: https://github.com/containerd/containerd/security/advisories/GHSA-rp3h-jf77-q9p4 and https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6796. On the release/2.3 branch the fix is commit https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/c535779652bc8d541328a36ba598088c09819b97 (archive: skip redundant opaque whiteout walks), which changes pkg/archive/tar.go and its test, and is in v2.3.5 but not v2.3.4. We read every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each package checked against the index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 that keeps its Go symbol table; we read its Go build information, its function table (which lists runtime.main in every build) and its raw bytes. trivy links containerd's unpacker: github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/pkg/archive.Apply, applyNaive and its closures are in the function table of every build. The build information lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 to v2.2.4 in 0.69.1-r0 to 0.70.0-r6, v2.3.1 to v2.3.3 in 0.71.0-r0 to 0.74.0-r4, which the advisory lists as affected, and v2.3.5 or later from 0.74.0-r5, with no replace directive for it; the source paths in each binary name the same version for pkg/archive/tar.go, v2.3.3 in 0.74.0-r4 and v2.3.5 in 0.74.0-r5. Builds 0.69.1-r0 to 0.70.0-r6 also list the older github.com/containerd/containerd module (1.7.29 to 1.7.32), but no function or source path from its archive package is in them. 0.74.0-r5 is the first build that carries the fix.

On the release/2.3 branch the fix is commit https://github.com/containerd/containerd/commit/c535779652bc8d541328a36ba598088c09819b97 (archive: skip redundant opaque whiteout walks), which changes pkg/archive/tar.go and its test, and is in v2.3.5 but not v2.3.4. We read every published trivy package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each package checked against the index checksum. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 that keeps its Go symbol table; we read its Go build information, its function table (which lists runtime.main in every build) and its raw bytes. trivy links containerd's unpacker: github.com/containerd/containerd/v2/pkg/archive.Apply, applyNaive and its closures are in the function table of every build. The build information lists github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 v2.2.0 to v2.2.4 in 0.69.1-r0 to 0.70.0-r6, v2.3.1 to v2.3.3 in 0.71.0-r0 to 0.74.0-r4, which the advisory lists as affected, and v2.3.5 or later from 0.74.0-r5, with no replace directive for it; the source paths in each binary name the same version for pkg/archive/tar.go, v2.3.3 in 0.74.0-r4 and v2.3.5 in 0.74.0-r5. Builds 0.69.1-r0 to 0.70.0-r6 also list the older github.com/containerd/containerd module (1.7.29 to 1.7.32), but no function or source path from its archive package is in them. 0.74.0-r5 is the first build that carries the fix.
